CVE-2026-33721.title: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications.  ...
CVE-2026-33721.description: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Starting in version 4.2 and prior to version 8.6.1, a heap-buffer-overflow write in MapServer’s SLD (Styled Layer Descriptor) parser lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker crash the MapServer process by sending a crafted SLD with more than 100 Threshold elements inside a ColorMap/Categorize structure (commonly reachable via WMS GetMap with SLD_BODY). Version 8.6.1 patches the issue.

CVE-2026-42030.title: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications.  ...
CVE-2026-42030.description: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From version 6.0 to before version 8.6.2, a reflected XSS vulnerability in MapServer's WMS server allows an unauthenticated attacker to inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript into the browser of any user who opens a crafted WMS URL. The vulnerability is triggered via FORMAT=application/openlayers combined with an unsanitized SRS parameter in WMS 1.3.0 requests. This issue has been patched in version 8.6.2.

CVE-2026-45104.title: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications.  ...
CVE-2026-45104.description: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 6.4.0 to before 8.6.3, msSLDParseUserStyle always calls _SLDApplyRuleValues(psRule, psLayer, 1); for any <Rule> carrying <ElseFilter/> — it assumes msSLDParseRule added one class. When the rule has no symbolizer (a structurally valid SLD), msSLDParseRule adds zero, and _SLDApplyRuleValues ends up indexing _class[-1], resulting in a NULL pointer dereference. A 200-byte well-formed SLD via the WMS SLD_BODY= parameter is enough to trigger this, no auth required. This vulnerability is fixed in 8.6.3.

CVE-2026-54354.title: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications.  ...
CVE-2026-54354.description: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.4, MapServer's PostGIS runtime filter translation in src/mappostgis.cpp and msPostGISLayerTranslateFilter() treats a filteritem as numeric when CONNECTIONTYPE POSTGIS and metadata such as gml_<item>_type=Integer are configured, but it does not verify that attacker-controlled CGI qstring or OGC API Features featureId input is a numeric literal. The unquoted input is concatenated into the generated PostgreSQL/PostGIS predicate, allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker with access to an affected query endpoint to bypass predicates, enumerate unintended records, perform boolean-based or time-based SQL injection, and increase database load. The issue does not by itself establish database modification capabilities. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.4.

CVE-2026-54355.title: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications.  ...
CVE-2026-54355.description: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 6.0 until 8.6.4, MapServer's OpenLayers HTML output for SERVICE=WMS&REQUEST=GetMap&FORMAT=application/openlayers reflects an attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-Host value received as HTTP_X_FORWARDED_HOST through msBuildOnlineResource(), processLine(), and the [mapserv_onlineresource] substitution in src/maputil.c and src/maptemplate.c without escaping it for a single-quoted JavaScript string. When the deployment trusts the forwarded header and does not configure a fixed ows_onlineresource or MS_ONLINERESOURCE value, embedded single quotes can escape the generated URL string. An unauthenticated attacker can craft a URL that executes arbitrary JavaScript in the MapServer site origin when opened by a victim, enabling access to sessions or tokens, same-origin data and requests, and actions as the victim. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.4.

CVE-2026-77323.title: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications.  ...
CVE-2026-77323.description: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, an unauthenticated reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in OGC API Features collection-items HTML output allows crafted offset or limit query parameter values from raw CGI request handling in src/mapogcapi.cpp to reach template.params.offset or template.params.limit. share/ogcapi/templates/html-bootstrap/collection-items.html inserts those values without quoting or escaping into a script element. A victim who follows a crafted request can have the script element terminated by attacker-controlled markup, causing arbitrary JavaScript to execute under the MapServer origin and enabling access to browser-session data, actions as the victim, and content manipulation. This issue is fixed in 8.6.5.

CVE-2026-77324.title: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications.  ...
CVE-2026-77324.description: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 4.4.0 until 8.6.5, an unauthenticated remote attacker can send a WCS GetCoverage XML POST request whose BoundingBox element omits the crs attribute, causing xmlGetProp() in src/mapwcs.cpp to return null. msWCSParseRequest() then calls string functions on the null value before normal WCS exception handling, crashing the CGI or FastCGI worker. The analogous KVP or GET path is not affected because it obtains a count-validated, non-null token. A single request can terminate one worker, and repeated requests can exhaust a fixed worker pool and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

CVE-2026-77325.title: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications.  ...
CVE-2026-77325.description: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 6.0 until 8.6.5, MapServer's WMS OpenLayers output, selected by FORMAT=application/openlayers or template=openlayers, substitutes a request-derived online-resource value into a single-quoted JavaScript string in src/maptemplate.c. The prior remediation for GHSA-xqj6-vjqr-33vv used msEscapeJSonLikeString() to protect the JavaScript string but did not neutralize angle brackets, so attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-Host or X-Forwarded-Proto values can still terminate the script element at the HTML parser layer. Deployments that expose attacker-controlled PATH_INFO or map= values reaching the same string are also affected. An unauthenticated attacker can cause arbitrary JavaScript to execute in a victim's browser under the MapServer origin when the victim loads the crafted output. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

CVE-2026-77326.title: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications.  ...
CVE-2026-77326.description: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 8.2.0 until 8.6.5, an unauthenticated attacker can send a WMS GetLegendGraphic request with a nonempty BBOX and repeated LAYER parameters to trigger a heap buffer overflow in msWMSDispatch() in src/mapwms.cpp. The handler appends synthesized entries to cgiRequestObj.ParamNames and cgiRequestObj.ParamValues at NumParams without retaining the arrays' capacity or reallocating them, while incrementing NumParams inside the loop. Once the parser's hidden capacity is exhausted, the writes pass the heap allocation boundary. A single request can corrupt heap memory and crash the process; code execution may be possible but was not demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

CVE-2026-77327.title: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications.  ...
CVE-2026-77327.description: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, MapServer's MySQL JOIN implementation in src/mapjoin.c copies the source layer attribute selected by JOIN ... FROM into joininfo->target and inserts it into the query built by msMySQLJoinNext() without parameterization or SQL escaping. When MySQL JOIN support is enabled, an attacker who can control that source feature attribute, including through imported shapefile or DBF data or another untrusted spatial source, can inject SQL operators or expressions that change the intended JOIN predicate. This can bypass the intended key comparison and expose unrelated records from the MySQL or MariaDB JOIN table through output templates, query responses, or downstream application logic. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

CVE-2026-77328.title: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications.  ...
CVE-2026-77328.description: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, MapServer's PostgreSQL JOIN implementation in src/mappostgresql.c copies the source layer attribute selected by JOIN FROM into joininfo->from_value and embeds it without parameterization or escaping into a dynamically generated PostgreSQL query executed by PQexec(). When PostgreSQL JOIN support is enabled, an attacker who can control that source feature attribute can inject quote characters and SQL operators that alter the intended WHERE predicate. This second-order injection can cause unintended rows and JOIN attributes to be returned, potentially exposing information from unrelated PostgreSQL records. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.
